sections.title: Category Management: Strategy
paragraphs: • Strategy Summary - displays an overview of the strategy,

sections.title: Category Management: Strategy Details Tab
paragraphs: • Strategy Settings: includes selected categories, business units and regions, along with
time information such as planned start date and planned end date.
• Strategy Team : a team of users who perform different roles within the strategy.
• Attachments: allows you to attach documents, such as those that apply to or may
facilitate the execution of the strategy.
• History of Changes: provides an audit log for changes made to the strategy and its

sections.title: Category Management: Strategy
paragraphs: • Analysis: describe key requirements, impacts and challenges and business needs of
the strategy. This is an optional activity but it can be very useful for providing focus and
helping determine activities and methods for executing the strategy.
• Spend : analyze category spend in terms of both volume and cost. A data file with
spend related to the categories is imported and the contents are then displayed in pre-
defined fields and charts that assist you in understanding usage.
• Demand Forecast: understanding and predicting future demands for goods and
services and their impact on supply decisions. On this page you may import a
forecasting file, the contents of which are displaying in pre-defined fields and charts,
similar to the Spend analysis page.

sections.title: Category Management: Strategy
paragraphs: • Lever Selection: allows you to select the methods that you will utilize to
execute the strategy. Those methods are automatically attached to a specific
Lever, and the Levers are connected to one of four Purchasing Strategies
• Supplier Portfolio: a collection of value-adding analyses and actions
needed to manage supplier expectations and achieve category strategies.

sections.title: Category Management: Strategy
paragraphs: • Implementation Documentation: documenting planned activities. These
documents can be uploaded and attached, allowing users to reference them while
• Activity Planning: mechanisms by which a strategy is executed. Some of these
activities are RFQs, RFIs, Auction, Contract, Saving Initiative, and Supplier Plans.
• Strategy Approval: allows the strategy details to be sent to other users for approval
before it is activated. This is an optional task.

sections.title: Key Terms:Key Terms:
paragraphs: Choosing this setting will allow all supplier responses to be accessible to
the buyer and project team as soon as they are submitted, regardless of
the closing date or order. Sealed (Parallel Opening)
Choosing this setting will keep all supplier responses sealed until the
closing date/time has passed. At that time, all 3 envelopes may be
accessed in any order. Sealed (Sequential Opening)
Choosing this setting will keep all supplier responses sealed until the
closing date/time has passed. At that time, the first envelope available
for review and evaluation is the Qualification envelope. Once evaluation
for that type of envelope has been frozen, the reviewers may move on to
the Technical envelope responses, etc. This setting is Best Practice.
